lines.text: Thanks for telling me. You don't have to sort it all out right now. We could slow your breathing for a minute, find a meeting, or keep talking here. If you're not safe right now, tap I'm not safe or call 000.
lines.spoken: Thanks for telling me. You don't have to sort it all out right now. We could slow your breathing for a minute, find a meeting, or keep talking here. If you're not safe right now, tap I'm not safe or call triple zero.

lines.text: Cravings for a drink, a use or a bet rise and fall, and this one can pass. Try to wait 15 minutes before you decide anything. Slow breathing can help, so can calling your sponsor or someone in your circle, or getting to a meeting. If you're not safe right now, tap I'm not safe or call 000.

lines.text: Lifeline 24/7 crisis support for anyone in Australia who is feeling overwhelmed or finding it hard to cope. 24 hours. Call 13 11 14 You can also text 0477 13 11 14. Call 13 11 14 Text 0477 13 11 14 More info Short-term, confidential support from a trained crisis supporter, including if you're thinking about suicide or worried about someone. Call 13 11 14, text 0477 13 11 14 or chat online. All three are open 24/7. lifeline.org.au Beyond Blue Free counselling for anxiety, depression or feeling overwhelmed, for anyone in Australia. 24 hours. Call 1300 22 4636 Call 1300 22 4636 More info Counsellors listen and help you find the right mental health services. You can also call if you're supporting a partner, family member or friend. Call 1300 22 4636 or use webchat, both 24/7. Free and confidential. Local call costs apply on the phone. On webchat you don't have to give your real name. beyondblue.org.au Suicide Call Back Service Free 24/7 counselling for anyone affected by suicide, aged 15 and over. 24 hours. Call 1300 659 467 For anyone thinking about suicide, worried about someone, or grieving a suicide. Call 1300 659 467 More info For people feeling suicidal, worried about or caring for someone, or who have lost someone to suicide. Also for emotional or mental health issues. Phone and online chat are 24/7. Video chat is by appointment (18 and over). Free, for people living in Australia. No referral needed. suicidecallbackservice.org.au 13YARN Free 24/7 crisis support for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Crisis Supporters. 24 hours. Call 13 92 76 Crisis support from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. Call 13 92 76 More info A confidential, culturally safe place to yarn if you're feeling worried or no good, or worried about someone you know. Call 13 92 76 24/7. Text 0447 13 92 76, or type to them online, 4pm to midnight every day. Free and confidential. 13yarn.org.au QLife Free, anonymous LGBTIQ+ peer support for talking about sexuality, gender, bodies, feelings or relationships. 3pm to 9pm local time, every day. Call 1800 184 527 LGBTIQ+ peer support. Not a crisis line. Out of hours, call Lifeline 13 11 14. Call 1800 184 527 More info Run by LGBTIQA+SB people. Family members, friends and others who support someone LGBTIQA+SB are welcome too. Phone or webchat, 3pm to 9pm your local time, every day including holidays. Last calls are taken by 8.40pm. Free and anonymous. Not a crisis line. qlife.org.au National Alcohol and Other Drug Hotline Free, confidential support for anyone worried about their own or someone else's alcohol or drug use. Call 1800 250 015 Connects you to your state's alcohol and drug service. Open 24/7, except South Australia (8.30am to 10pm). In an emergency call 000, or Lifeline 13 11 14 any time. Call 1800 250 015 More info Your call goes through to the alcohol and drug service in your state or territory. Open 24/7. From South Australia, the service runs 8.30am to 10pm. Free and confidential. Run by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing. health.gov.au Adis 24/7 Alcohol and Drug Support (QLD) 24/7 confidential alcohol and drug support for Queenslanders and the people who care about them. Call 1800 177 833 Queensland only. Call 1800 177 833 More info For people in Queensland with alcohol or drug concerns, their loved ones, and health professionals. Call 24/7, chat online with a counsellor, or request a call back. There's also an SMS support program. adis.health.qld.gov.au National Gambling Helpline Free, confidential 24/7 support for anyone affected by gambling, yours or someone else's. 24 hours. Call 1800 858 858 Free and confidential, anywhere in Australia. Not run by Gamblers Anonymous. Call 1800 858 858 More info Talk to a trained counsellor any time, day or night, from anywhere in Australia. Gambling Help Online also has live chat and email support, free and confidential. Government funded. Not run by Gamblers Anonymous. gamblinghelponline.org.au AA Australia Talk to a sober member of Alcoholics Anonymous, any time, if drinking is a problem for you. 24 hours. Call 1300 222 222 Call 1300 222 222 More info Call the 24-hour helpline to speak with a sober alcoholic. You can also chat live with a member on the AA website, or find an in-person or online meeting. aa.org.au NA Australia Talk to a member of Narcotics Anonymous, or find a meeting near you. Call 1300 652 820 Call 1300 652 820 More info Call 1300 652 820 to find someone to talk to. Hours aren't published. To find meetings, text your suburb or postcode and state (for example, Paddington QLD) to 0488 811 247 and you'll get a list of meetings nearby. na.org.au

lines.text: Keep your details private Don't share your full name, address, phone, bank details or passwords with anyone in HomeCircle or at meetings. Real friends and sponsors won't ask for money or private details. If someone does, tell your sponsor or a trusted person. Code of conduct Be kind. At meetings you find through HomeCircle, please respect that group's own guidelines, and don't record or share what people say. Questions or concerns? Email us, and we aim to reply within 24 hours. HomeCircle is support, not medical care.

lines.text: Have this read to you Your phone can read any page out loud, including this one. iPhone or iPad: go to Settings > Accessibility > Read & Speak (on older versions, Spoken Content) and turn on Speak Screen. Then swipe down with two fingers from the top of the screen, or say “Siri, speak screen”. Android: go to Settings > Accessibility > Select to Speak and turn on the Select to Speak shortcut. Tap the shortcut, then tap what you want read. If you can’t find it, install Android Accessibility Suite from Google Play.
